newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up led by blue chip.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up led by blue chip.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed up on Thursday due to foreign buying of a highly capitalised blue chip, brokers said.
The all share index closed 2.74 points up at 625.56. Losses led gains by 27 to 18 but blue-chip John keells Holdings, up four rupees to 194, supporting the index.

Turnover was 14.07 million rupees on 495,919 shares led by foreign buying of 18,500 John Keells Holdings Ltd, 30,700 Distilleries Co of Sri Lanka Ltd and local buying of 23,400 Kotagala Plantations Ltd, 120,000 Ceylon Holiday Resorts Ltd.
"There is more foreign buying waiting to emerge after this month because investors want to see if elections will affect prices," said Gordon Nadesan, a trader at brokerage CT Smith.
Investors believe any violence ahead of March 21 local government polls could depress prices.
Brokers also say investors are refocusing on hotel stocks. "Investors are looking at hotels because tourist arrivals in the current quarter are better than in previous times," said one.
Tourism was hit in 1995 and 1996 after Tamil rebel attacks in the capital including the blowing up of a suburban oil depot and a suicide bomb blast in the heart of the financial district.
